archetype.name: Better Than Its Record (lottery-bound)
archetype.definition: A team whose point margin and defense say it is closer to a fringe Eastern team than a bottom-four one, but whose offense, without its injured lead guard, is too thin to climb far out of the lottery.

report.headline: A real defensive reset, buried under broken shooting and Haliburton's absence
report.take:
Indiana at 5-12 looks like a repeat of last season's 19-63 collapse, but the underlying team is different. Last year's group posted a Net Rtg of -7.9 with the 24th-ranked defense. This one sits at -3.8, 20th in the league, and its defense has climbed to 16th with a 114.8 DRtg, essentially league average. The margin implies 7 wins, not 5, and the W vs Pt Diff of -2 ranks 26th. Close games have gone against them: one-possession losses to Atlanta and Dallas sit in the last 10. This is a below-average team, not a bottom-feeder.

The problem is the offense, 26th with a 111 ORtg. Its shape is specific. The Pacers shoot 32.8% from three, 29th in the league and well below last year's 35.6%, while taking fewer threes than the league norm. They also chase almost none of their own misses: ORB % of 20.8 ranks dead last. Pascal Siakam carries the load with 370 points at a 28.5 USG % and 59.6 TS %. The supporting cast around him is where it breaks down. Tyrese Haliburton played 4 games with a 7.9 BPM and a +10.2 On-Off before going Out, and the offense has had no organizer of that level since.

The roster grades show where the losses come from. The backcourt holds a B-, propped up by Quenton Jackson's efficient minutes and Andrew Nembhard's playmaking. The wings (D) and frontcourt (D-) are sinking it. Aaron Nesmith has played the most wing minutes with a 49.4 TS %, a -5 BPM and a -12 On-Off. Jarace Walker's 45.1 TS % is the worst among the regulars. The defense is decent at the rim, fifth in Opp Rim FG %, but small forwards have torched it: 27.24 points a game allowed to SFs, 30th in the league. That is another symptom of the wing problem.

The direction is not encouraging in the short run. October's offense scored 116.67 a game; November's managed 108.91. The last five games went 1-4 at -7.2 a game, though four of them came against Philadelphia, Houston, Cleveland and New York. Some relief should come naturally: opponents are hitting 37.4% from three, 26th, after the defense held teams to 35.5% last year. The ceiling, though, depends on Haliburton, and the sheet only says he is out.

strengths.title: Defense rebuilt around rim protection
strengths.body: The DRtg of 114.8 ranks 16th, a real step up from last season's 118.8 and 24th-place finish. The core of it is the paint: opponents shoot 61.9% at the rim (5th) and take a below-average share of shots there. That structural change should hold. The only thing dragging the overall number down is opponents' three-point shooting, which is the noisier part of defense.

strengths.title: Siakam as a reliable engine
strengths.body: Siakam leads the team in minutes and points (370) and keeps his efficiency at a 59.6 TS % while using 28.5% of possessions. He ranks 14th on the PF tab and is the frontcourt's only above-average regular. That production is the most dependable thing on the roster.

strengths.title: Margin better than the record
strengths.body: The point differential implies 7 wins against the actual 5, and the Net Rtg ranks 20th, several spots above where the record sits. Close-game results tend to even out. Some wins should come back without any change in how the team plays.

concerns.title: Shooting and second chances both missing
concerns.body: A 32.8% mark from three (29th) and a league-worst 20.8 ORB % leave the offense with neither efficient first shots nor extra ones, hence the 26th-ranked ORtg. The three-point percentage should drift up toward last year's level. The offensive rebounding looks like a roster trait, since it was also low last season.

concerns.title: Wings losing their minutes badly
concerns.body: The wing group grades a D. Nesmith has played the most minutes there with a -12 On-Off and a 49.4 TS %, and Oubre is at -7. On defense, opposing small forwards are scoring 27.24 a game, the most in the league. Jalen Slawson's +12.8 On-Off in limited minutes suggests the rotation itself is part of the fix.

concerns.title: No Haliburton, no shot creation
concerns.body: In 4 games Haliburton posted a 63.4 TS % and a +10.2 On-Off, and he ranks 7th on the PG tab. He is listed Out. Without him, the offensive burden falls on Siakam and a committee of guards who play efficiently but at low usage.

trend.note: A 2-4 October with a competitive offense gave way to a 3-8 November in which scoring fell to 108.91 a game. The last five games went 1-4, with defense slipping to 119 allowed a game, against a demanding run of opponents.

weekAhead.headline: Two home tests, then a winnable trip to Chicago
weekAhead.body:
The week opens at home against Oklahoma City, which has the league's best rim defense and the 5th-best DRtg. That is a brutal matchup for an offense that already can't shoot from outside. Philadelphia comes next. Its 14-3 record leans heavily on close games, with the league's top W vs Pt Diff at 4 and a Net Rtg of only 3. Indiana lost 124-131 in Philadelphia this month, so that game is more winnable than the standings suggest.

The week closes in Chicago. The Bulls are a fellow cellar team with the 28th-ranked defense, and they concede rim shots and point-guard production in bulk. A 1-2 week is the baseline. A 2-1 week depends on stealing the Philadelphia game at home.

keyMatchups.title: Indiana's offense against OKC's paint wall
keyMatchups.body: Oklahoma City allows 56.7% at the rim, the best mark in the league, and posts a 110.5 DRtg. Indiana's offense already struggles from three, so OKC takes away the inside options Siakam and Zubac rely on. Scoring will be very hard to come by.

keyMatchups.title: Siakam against Philadelphia's power forwards
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia allows power forwards 3.24 points above their usual output, a rank of 27th. That is the exact spot where Indiana's best scorer lives. The 76ers' record also overstates them, so a big Siakam night could swing a home upset.

keyMatchups.title: Indiana's guards against Chicago's leaky backcourt
keyMatchups.body: Chicago concedes 30.94 points a game to point guards, 29th in the league, plus the most threes at the position. It also allows the league's highest Opp Rim Rate. Jackson, Nembhard and Smith should find room, and this is the game Indiana is built to win.

weekAhead.watch: Whether the three-point shooting finally turns, especially against Chicago's 23rd-ranked perimeter defense, or whether the offense stays stuck regardless of opponent.

restOfSeason.body:
The defense looks real and should hold near league average. If opponents' three-point shooting cools toward last season's levels, it could improve a little. The offense is the variable. Shooting this poor rarely persists across a full season, so a modest rebound toward 33.5-35% from three is likely and would lift the Net Rtg. The structural gaps would remain: the worst offensive rebounding in the league, and wings who give back minutes. My projection has the Net Rtg settling around -2.5 to -5 and a final record of roughly 25 to 31 wins. That is comfortably better than last season but still lottery territory, with the current pace of 24 wins as the floor if nothing changes.

The upside case runs through Haliburton. His four games showed the offense functioning with him, and the sheet gives no timeline for his return. Until he comes back, expect a team that loses more games than its margin says it should and hovers near the bottom of the Central behind Detroit and Cleveland.
swingFactors: Haliburton's return and how many games he plays
Rotation changes on the wing (Nesmith's minutes vs Slawson's)

confidence.note: 17 games is a small sample, and Haliburton's status is unknown. The differential and defensive data are consistent enough to read.
